response.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT film_id, COUNT(actor_id) AS n
  FROM film_actor
  GROUP BY film_id
),
avg1 AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) AS a FROM counts
),
above1 AS (
  SELECT c.film_id, c.n, c.n - a1.a AS ex1
  FROM counts c
  CROSS JOIN avg1 a1
  WHERE c.n > a1.a
),
avg2 AS (
  SELECT AVG(n) AS b FROM above1
),
kept AS (
  SELECT x.film_id, x.n, x.ex1, x.n - a2.b AS ex2
  FROM above1 x
  CROSS JOIN avg2 a2
  WHERE x.n > a2.b
)
SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actors,
       AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first,
       AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second
FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: Actor count per film is COUNT(actor_id) over film_art rows; the composite primary key (actor_id, film_id) guarantees each actor is counted once per film.
Films with no film_actor rows are excluded by grouping on film_actor, so they never enter either average.

If either average is NULL (for example, no qualifying films), the comparison `n > avg` is never true, so no films are kept. The final SUM and AVG then return NULL, which is the SQL representation of a missing value. Returning 0 instead would be a different choice.
The second average is taken over the films kept after the first filter, as the request states, and the 'excess' values are unrounded differences.
